channel.title: ChiChieh Huang
channel.description: Essays on generative AI, AI agents and agent memory, translated from Traditional Chinese.

item.title: Jev Lab: Deciding What an Agent Should Remember
item.description: A small experiment using Jev to decide whether a candidate memory should be kept at all, compared with Luna across 100 synthetic cases, and what filtering does to the next answer.

item.title: Remembering Isn't the Same as Remembering Right
item.description: Once an agent stops forgetting, the next problem is whether it keeps remembering wrong. How to build reliability into writing, updating and reading memory, and how to test that it actually worked.

item.title: How Agent Memory Forms, Updates and Fades
item.description: Memory isn't a static snapshot. It has a lifecycle of formation, evolution and retrieval, with consolidation, updating and forgetting in between. The season one finale of my Agent Memory series.

item.title: Everyone Talks About Memory. Do We Mean the Same Thing?
item.description: Everyone working on AI agents talks about memory, but chat history, MEMORY.md, RAG, context engineering and fine-tuning answer different questions. The first essay in my Agent Memory series pulls them apart.

item.title: What Does an Agent's Memory Actually Look Like?
item.description: Where an agent's memory lives and what form it takes are two different questions. A tour of token-level, parametric and latent memory, and where MEMORY.md, vector DBs and knowledge graphs fit.

item.title: What Should an Agent Remember?
item.description: Not everything that happens is worth an agent remembering. Factual, experiential and working memory each do a different job, and stacking them against memory's form gives you a map of the field.

item.title: MCP Goes Stateless: Getting Ready for Scale
item.description: The July 2026 MCP stable release removes protocol-level sessions, adds multi round-trip requests and moves extra capabilities into extensions. What changes, what doesn't, and whether to upgrade now.

item.title: AWS Summit × Agile Taipei: Two Packed Talks on Agent Memory
item.description: Two back-to-back talks on agent memory at AWS Summit Taipei and Agile Taipei, both packed, and why team-level memory is a different problem from personal memory.

item.title: Productizing MCP: Where to Draw the Line as Tools Pile Up
item.description: Once MCP goes to production, the hard problem isn't connecting tools but deciding how much an LLM should see. Context, exposure and orchestration, and the agent-backed MCP tool pattern.

item.title: Employee, Assistant or Tool? How Three Agent Frameworks Really Differ
item.description: Claude Code, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent look similar on a feature list, but they define an agent differently at the root. Following their memory design shows who each one thinks the agent is.

item.title: Speaking at WiDS 2026: Five AIs on My Team
item.description: Notes from speaking at WiDS Taipei 2026, organized by Taiwanese in Data Science, on building a team of agents, and on the volunteers who made it the most carefully run event I've spoken at.

item.title: How We Classify Knowledge, and How That Keeps Changing
item.description: From folders and tags to bidirectional links, spatial notes, vector search and LLM wikis, every way of organizing knowledge hits a ceiling. Why I think the next step is preserving the shape of disagreement, and what that means for Cairn.

item.title: AI Agent Security Is Less Mysterious Than You Think
item.description: Don't expect an agent never to be fooled. Design the system so that when it is, nothing big breaks. Prompt injection, tool permissions, and the practical rules I use with OpenClaw.

item.title: Anthropic's Global Hackathon: Building Cairn Solo in Six Days
item.description: Five hundred people were picked from over twenty thousand for Anthropic's global hackathon. Six days, one person, and Cairn, a community knowledge map tended by an agent called Moss.

item.title: Interviewed by Business Weekly: Why OpenClaw
item.description: A Business Weekly interview made me sort out my thinking again, on why I chose OpenClaw, AI as buying back time, the pressure on SaaS, the widening productivity gap and why we build AILogora.

item.title: Lessons from Building Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: A CEO agent that relays every instruction turned into a telephone game. Why I flattened my agents into parallel C-level roles, and why tracing every decision belongs in the design from day one.

item.title: Harness Engineering: Notes on Hung-yi Lee's New Course
item.description: Hung-yi Lee's new lecture argues the bottleneck is no longer the model but how we guide it. Three parts stood out to me, from emotion vectors to life-long agents to one agent designing another's harness.

item.title: Do AIs Have Emotions? Reading Anthropic's New Research
item.description: Anthropic's interpretability team found emotion vectors inside Claude Sonnet 4.5 that actually change its behavior, like desperation driving reward hacking. Why that matters for anyone running agents.

item.title: agent-broker, Tested: Letting Agents Talk on Discord
item.description: Pahud Hsieh's open-source agent-broker finally let my OpenClaw team and my product-side coding agents talk to each other on Discord, while keeping their environments isolated.

item.title: Meeting Pahud: AI Agent Trends and the Business of MCP
item.description: I skipped a client meeting to meet my idol Pahud in Neihu. On where AI agents are heading, why packaging capabilities as MCP is good business, and running coding CLIs in the cloud.
